This topic introduces how to use the Web Viewer SDK to run demos that automatically play videos in a video list on phones and PCs.

<span id="85745c1c"></span>
## Introduction

After running the demos, you can swipe up and down or left and right on phones, or scroll up and down or left and right on PCs to browse the video list.


<Tabs>
<Tab zoneid="M5fLHlAseY" title="Demos for phones">
<TabTitle>Demos for phones</TabTitle>

When a player is fully displayed, the live video, preview, or playback will automatically play. If a live room has no live video, preview, or playback, the cover image will be displayed.

The demos automatically play a specific number of videos by default. You can customize your code to adjust the number.


* Demo for swiping up and down: By default, only the first two fully displayed players automatically play videos simultaneously.

* Demo for swiping left and right: By default, only the first fully displayed player automatically plays the video simultaneously.


</Tab>
<Tab zoneid="yA989QhQic" title="Demos for PCs">
<TabTitle>Demos for PCs</TabTitle>

When viewers open the web page, the first player in the list automatically plays the video. When they hover over any other player, that player starts playing the video automatically. After viewers stop hovering over all players, the last hovered player’s video continues playing.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">If a live room has no live video, preview, or playback, the cover image will be displayed.</div>



</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Prerequisites


* An IAM user with the super administrator role. For more information, see [Managing users, organizations, and roles](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-managing-iam-users-and-roles).

* Get the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key of the IAM user for API request authentication.

   1. Log in to the [BytePlus Live console](https://console.byteplus.com/livesaas/liveManagement/) with the IAM user.

   2. Click your avatar in the upper\-right corner and select **IAM** in the dropdown list.

   3. On the left navigation pane, click **Access Key Management**.

   4. Get the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.

      <div style="text-align: center">
      <img src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/c1200b9225414a469a6626a161a520bc~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" width="1883px" />      </div>
      


<span id="3e1ef720"></span>
## Process


<Tabs>
<Tab zoneid="YeNrzFj41q" title="Demo for swiping up and down on phones">
<TabTitle>Demo for swiping up and down on phones</TabTitle>

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/5342055bbef844d48e748fc14b9bc735~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


1. Initialize your server and load the cache on the server.

   To load specific live rooms when viewers tap a tab on the web page, see [Classifying live rooms](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#f39a511c).

2. Call [ListActivityFeedInfosAPI](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/byteplus-livesaas/listactivityfeedinfosapi) on your server in a loop to get all the live rooms in this demo in real time.

3. After each API call, the BytePlus Live server returns data to your server.

4. Store the returned data in the local cache on your server.

5. When viewers swipe up and down the web page in your app and the page number changes, you must call your in\-house API to load live rooms from the local cache on your server. We provide an example of such an API for reference. For more information, see [In-house API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#5dcd303c).

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">tip   </div>
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-wrapper-indent="1">This demo has latency when changing the live room status. To reduce such latency, you must call <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/byteplus-livesaas/activitystatusmodifycallback">ActivityStatusModifyCallBack</a>. When the live room status changes, BytePlus Live sends a GET request to your custom URL used to receive the callback and passes the new status in the query string. Then, you can update the live room status.   </div>
   

6. Your server returns data to your app's WebView.

7. Get player keys.

   <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

   1. When viewers swipe up and down the web page on phones, you can call [Intersection Observer API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Intersection_Observer_API) to store the keys of the players fully displayed during the swipe.

   2. When viewers stop swiping the web page, you can listen for the [scrollend](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/scrollend_event) event to read the stored player keys and get the keys, such as 0 and 1, of the first two fully displayed players on the current page.

8. Play videos or destroy players.

   <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

   1. Iterate through the list of keys and compare whether the keys of the first two fully displayed players on the current page match the keys of the initialized players.

      * Matches: Indicates that the player is not destroyed, so play the video directly.

      * Does not match: Indicates that the player is destroyed. In this case, check if the length of the player queue is less than or equal to 20. You can customize the value, but for optimal user experience, we recommend that the value is no greater than 20.

         * Less than or equal to 20: Create a player at the end of the queue and play the video. The player queue is then updated.

         * Greater than 20: Destroy the player at the beginning of the queue first, then create a player at the end of the queue and play the video. The player queue is then updated.

   2. When a player is about to be destroyed, you can draw the paused frame of the player using Canvas. After the player is destroyed, store the player's paused time (`currentTime`) and read the time when creating a player. When the video is about to automatically play, load the previously drawn paused frame and play the video from the `currentTime`, achieving the effect of resuming playback from the last paused point.

      <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

      In this demo, you can store the `currentTime` of at most 50 players. You can also customize the value, but for optimal performance, we recommend that the value is no greater than 50.


<span id="54f90f7e"></span>
### Classifying live rooms

To load specific live rooms when viewers tap a tab on the web page, you can use one of the following solutions:


* Solution A

   1. Add category tag values to live rooms on the BytePlus Live console. For more information, see [Tagging live rooms](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-tagging-live-streams).

   2. Call [ListActivityFeedInfosAPI](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/byteplus-livesaas/listactivityfeedinfosapi) on your server in a loop to get all the live rooms, including the category tags in each live room. You can use the returned category tag values as tab names on the web page if needed.

   3. After each API call, the BytePlus Live server returns data to your server.

   4. Store the returned data in the local cache on your server.

   5. When viewers tap a tab on the web page, call your in\-house API with the `ActivityTag` value set to the category tag value corresponding to the tab. This will load live rooms with the specified category tag value from the local cache on your server. For more information, see [In-house API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#5dcd303c).

* Solution B

   1. When initializing your server, save the mapping between tags and live rooms on the server.

   2. When viewers tap a tab on the web page, call your in\-house API with the `ActivityTag` value set to the tag corresponding to the tab. This will load live rooms with the specified tag from your server. For more information, see [In-house API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#5dcd303c).

* Solution C

   1. Save the mapping between tags and live rooms on the server when initializing your server. In addition, add category tag values to live rooms on the BytePlus Live console.

   2. Call [ListActivityFeedInfosAPI](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/byteplus-livesaas/listactivityfeedinfosapi) on your server in a loop to get all the live rooms, including the category tags in each live room. You can use the returned category tag values as tab names on the web page if needed.

   3. After each API call, the BytePlus Live server returns data to your server.

   4. Store the returned data in the local cache on your server.

   5. When viewers tap a tab on the web page, call your in\-house API with the `ActivityTag` value set to the category tag value or tag corresponding to the tab. This will load live rooms with the specified category tag value or tag from your server. For more information, see [In-house API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#5dcd303c).


</Tab>

<span id="88f7f2e4"></span>
## Procedure

<span id="4aa2fcf7"></span>
### Demos for phones

To speed up the loading of the demo and save WebView resource request time, the static resources required by the demo are directly packaged into the React Native app.

Here, use an Android project as an example.


1. Contact BytePlus Live technical support to get the React Native source code and make sure that the directory structure under `android/app/src/main/assets/public` is as follows:

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/fdf5c2d9077f417c832907d0035e5711~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

   ```Plain
   |-- assets/public
       |-- assert // SDK resources required by the demo
           |-- mobile  // SDK resources required by the detail page
           |-- player-mobile // SDK resources required by the list page
       |-- static // Static resources generated during demo development
   ```
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">warning   </div>
   

   * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">Make sure the directory structure is under the <code>assets</code> directory.   </div>
   

   * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">You can customize your web page by changing the demo source code. Contact BytePlus Live technical support to get the source code.   </div>
   

   * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">In the <code>mobile</code> directory, <code>.js</code> files support code splitting, which can reduce JS parsing time and thereby decrease the blank screen duration when navigating from the list page to the detail page.   </div>
   

2. Create the HTML template file for the list page.

   In the root directory of the project, create a file named `websdkListHtml.ts`. Export the HTML template for rendering the WebView in React Native.

   The content of the `websdkListHtml.ts` file is as follows.

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">warning   </div>
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">Make sure that the reference paths for static resources start with the <code>file</code> protocol, namely <code>file:///android_asset</code>.   </div>
   

   ```HTML
   export default `
   <!doctype html>
   <html lang="en">
       <head>
           <meta charset="UTF-8" />
           <meta
               name="viewport"
               content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1,minimum-scale=1,maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no,shrink-to-fit=no,viewport-fit=cover"
           />
           <link
               rel="stylesheet"
               href="file:///android_asset/public/assert/player-mobile/index.2.0.6-beta.13.css"
           />
           <title>Demo</title>
   ```

3. In the app's WebView, use the HTML template for the list page.

   
   <Tabs>
   <Tab zoneid="jFJS7IHQlE" title="Demo for swiping up and down">
   <TabTitle>Demo for swiping up and down</TabTitle>
   
   ```TypeScript
   import websdklistHtml from './websdkListHtml'
   
   <WebView
     originWhitelist={['*']}
     scalesPageToFit={false}
     useWebKit={true}
     javaScriptEnabled
     allowFileAccess={true}
     allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs={true}
     onMessage={event => {
       const { ActivityId, ActivityInfo } = JSON.parse(
         event.nativeEvent.data,
       );
       if (!selectRoom || ActivityId !== selectRoom.activityId) {
         setTimeout(() => {
           setSelectRoom({
             activityId: ActivityId,
             token: ActivityInfo.SdkToken,
           });
         }, 0);
       } 
     }}
     source={{
       html: websdklistHtml,
       baseUrl:
         'https://live.byteplus.com?playCount=2&maxCount=20&maxStoreCount=50&hideTab=1',
     }}
   />
   ```
   
   
   Where,
   
   
      * The value of `playCount` can be either `1` or `2`, indicating that 1 or 2 videos can automatically play at a time.
   
      * The value of `maxCount` is an integer within the range of [2, 20], representing the length of the player queue. For more information about the length of the player queue, see step 8 in [Process](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#3e1ef720).
   
      * The value of `maxStoreCount` is an integer equal to or less than 50, representing the number of players whose paused time (`currentTime`) can be written to local storage of Web Viewer SDK after players are destroyed. For more information about `currentTime`, see step 8 in [Process](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#3e1ef720).
   
      * To hide all the tabs on the web page and display all the live rooms in the list, set the value of `hideTab` to `1`. To display the tabs on the web page, do not include the `hideTab` parameter.
   
   
   </Tab>
   <Tab zoneid="Eop40dy9Lx" title="Demo for swiping left and right">
   <TabTitle>Demo for swiping left and right</TabTitle>
   
   ```TypeScript
   import websdklistHtml from './websdkListHtml'
   
   <WebView
     originWhitelist={['*']}
     scalesPageToFit={false}
     useWebKit={true}
     javaScriptEnabled
     allowFileAccess={true}
     allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs={true}
     onMessage={event => {
       const { ActivityId, ActivityInfo } = JSON.parse(
         event.nativeEvent.data,
       );
       if (!selectRoom || ActivityId !== selectRoom.activityId) {
         setTimeout(() => {
           setSelectRoom({
             activityId: ActivityId,
             token: ActivityInfo.SdkToken,
           });
         }, 0);
       } 
     }}
     source={{
       html: websdklistHtml,
       baseUrl:
         'https://live.byteplus.com/carouselList?playCount=2&maxCount=20&maxStoreCount=50&itemWidth=100&itemHeight=100',
     }}
   />
   ```
   
   
   Where,
   
   
      * The value of `playCount` can be either `1` or `2`, indicating that 1 or 2 videos can automatically play at a time.
   
      * The value of `maxCount` is an integer within the range of [2, 20], representing the length of the player queue. For more information about the length of the player queue, see step 8 in [Process](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#3e1ef720).
   
      * The value of `maxStoreCount` is an integer equal to or less than 50, representing the number of players whose paused time (`currentTime`) can be written to local storage of Web Viewer SDK after players are destroyed. For more information about `currentTime`, see step 8 in [Process](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#3e1ef720).
   
      * The value of `itemWidth` is an integer representing the width of the video in the video list. The default value is `220` and the unit is px.
   
      * The value of `itemHeight` is an integer representing the height of the video in the video list. The default value is `330` and the unit is px.
   
   
   </Tab>

4. Create the HTML template file for the detail page.

   In the root directory of the project, create a file named `websdkDetailHtml.ts`. Export the HTML template for rendering the WebView in React Native.

   The content of the `websdkDetailHtml.ts` file is as follows.

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">warning   </div>
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">Make sure that the reference paths for static resources start with the <code>file</code> protocol, namely <code>file:///android_asset</code>.   </div>
   

   ```HTML
   export default `<!DOCTYPE html>
               <html style="height: 100%">
                 <head>
                   <title>BytePlus Live Web SDK DEMO</title>
                   <link rel="shortcut icon"
                     href=//p16-live-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-j963mrpdmh/06d5d4d7332c0e08829eb780643c9019.png~tplv-j963mrpdmh-image.image
                     sizes="16x16">
                   <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1.0,minimum-scale=1.0,
                         maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no, shrink-to-fit=no, viewport-fit=cover">
                   <link rel="stylesheet"
                     href="file:///android_asset/public/assert/mobile/index.2.0.6-beta.13.css">
                   <style>
                     .app {
                       height: 100%;
                       width: 100%;
                     }
                   </style>
                 </head>
   
                 <body style='
                       font-size: 10px; margin: 0; overflow: hidden;
                       height: 100%;'>
                   <div id='app' class="app"></div>
                   <script src="file:///android_asset/public/assert/mobile/index.2.0.6-beta.13.js"></script>
                   </body>
                   <script>
                     var url = window.location;
                     var params = new URLSearchParams(url.search);
                     var webSDK = new window.ByteLiveWebSDK({
                       activityId: params.get('activityId') || 1733120****10066, // The activity ID of the live room.
                       
                       token: params.get('token') || 'ZQ****', // The user token.
                       service: 'liveDemo', 
                       mode: 1, // The authentication mode is public.
                       modules: [
                         {
                           id: "app", // The page element ID. The full-page module for the portrait mode of mobile devices will be embedded into this element.
                           mode: "mobile-portrait",
                         },
                       ],
                       options: {
                          origin: 'https://live.byteplus.com'
                       }
                     })
                     webSDK.on('error', console.log);
                   </script>
               </html>`;
   ```

5. In the app's WebView, use the HTML template for the detail page.

   ```TypeScript
       import websdkDetailHtml from './websdkDetailHtml'
       
       <WebView
         originWhitelist={['*']}
         scalesPageToFit={false}
         useWebKit={true}
         javaScriptEnabled
         allowFileAccess={true}
         allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs={true}
         allowsInlineMediaPlayback={true}
         mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction={false}
         allowsFullscreenVideo={true}
         ref={webviewWindow}

         }}

   ```
   

6. Implement navigation from the list page to the detail page.

   Use `@react-navigation/native` and `@react-navigation/native-stack` to handle page navigation and parameter passing.

   1. In the WebView of the list page, listen for click events on the web page and send the corresponding live room information to React Native.

   2. After receiving the information, React Native navigates to the detail page using the `navigation.navigate` method.

   3. In the WebView of the detail page, initialize the Web Viewer SDK with the received information to display the viewing page.


<span id="4a589b4e"></span>
### Demos for PCs

Contact BytePlus Live technical support to get the demo source code for the PC web page.


* To change the default settings of autoplay, add the following parameters to your web page URL as needed:

   * `autoPlayMode`: The mode of autoplay. The default value is `1`.

      * `1`: Unmuted autoplay.

      * `2`: Muted autoplay.

      * `3`: Do not play automatically. Viewers can only click a player to join the live room to watch the video. If the value is set to `3`, videos will not play automatically even if the value of `defaultFirstPlay` or `hoverPlay` is set to `true`.

      <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="2">tip      </div>
      

      <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-wrapper-indent="2">If the value is set to <code>1</code> but the video is muted during autoplay, or if the value is set to <code>1</code> or <code>2</code> but the video fails to play automatically, the possible reasons are as follows:      </div>
      

      * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-wrapper-indent="2">Viewers open the web page using the Safari browser and the browser does not allow autoplay. For more information on allowing autoplay in Safari, see Safari's official documentation.      </div>
      

      * <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-wrapper-indent="2">Due to browser autoplay policies, some browsers only allow muted autoplay. If a browser does not support either muted or unmuted autoplay, the video will not play automatically. For more information, see <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/autoplay/">Autoplay policy in Chrome</a>, <a href="https://webkit.org/blog/7734/auto-play-policy-changes-for-macos/">Auto\-Play Policy Changes for macOS</a>, and <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/zh-CN/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Autoplay">Autoplay guide</a>.      </div>
      

   * `hoverPlay`: Whether the video plays automatically when a viewer hovers over a player. The default value is `true`.

      * `true`: Play automatically.

      * `false`: Do not play automatically.

   * `defaultFirstPlay`: Whether the first player in the video list automatically plays the video when viewers open the web page. The default value is `true`. This parameter takes effect only when the value of `hoverPlay` is set to `true`.

      * `true`: Play automatically.

      * `false`: Do not play automatically.

   * `maxCount`: An integer within the range of [2, 20], representing the length of the player queue. For more information about the length of the player queue, see step 7 in [Process](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#3e1ef720).

   * `maxStoreCount`: An integer equal to or less than 20, representing the number of players whose paused time (`currentTime`) can be written to local storage of Web Viewer SDK after players are destroyed. For more information about `currentTime`, see step 7 in [Process](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#3e1ef720).

      For example, if you want muted autoplay, add `autoPlayMode=2` to the web page URL, such as

      `https://live.byteplus.com/demo/sdk/pc.grid.html?autoPlayMode=2`.

<span id="5dcd303c"></span>
## In\-house API

You must call your in\-house API to load live rooms from the local cache on your server when:


* Viewers swipe up and down the web page in your app, causing the page number to change.

* Viewers scroll up and down the web page in their PC browser, causing the page number to change.

* Viewers swipe left and right on the web page in your app.

* Viewers scroll left and right on the web page in their PC browser.


This section describes an example of such an API for reference.

Method: GET

<span id="1eacdad0"></span>
### Request parameters

<span id="7129c212"></span>
#### Query


|Name |Data Type |Required |Sample Value |Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|PageNumber |String |No |`1` |The number of the page to return. Default value: `1`. The value must be equal to or greater than 1. |
|PageSize |String |No |`10` |The number of results to return on each page. Default value: `10`. Value range: [1,100]. |
|ActivityName |String |No |`A` |The live room name, which supports fuzzy search and is case insensitive. The name must be between 1 and 150 characters in length.<br><br>For example, if the parameter value is `A`, then live rooms with names containing `A`, such as `A`, `a`, and `Live room A`, are returned. |
|ActivityTag |String |No |`clothes` |The category tag value or tag used to load specific live rooms when viewers tap or click a tab on the web page.<br><br>If not configured, all live rooms will be returned.<br><br>This parameter only takes effect in the demo for swiping up and down on phones and the demo for scrolling up and down on PCs. |


<span id="f310317a"></span>
### Response parameters


|Name |Data Type |Sample Value |Description |
|---|---|---|---|
|PageNumber |Integer |`1` |The page number of the returned page. |
|PageSize |Integer |`10` |The number of results returned on each page. |
|TotalCount |Integer |`1` |The total number of returned live rooms. |
|List |Array of [List](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#b36ac446) |`-` |List of returned live rooms. |


<span id="b36ac446"></span>
#### List


|Name |Data Type |Sample Value |Description |
|---|---|---|---|
|ActivityId |Long |`17218346****` |The activity ID of the returned live room. |
|ActivityInfo |Object of [ActivityInfo](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#bb44f8f9) |`-` |The information of the returned live room. |
|ActivityData |Object of [ActivityData](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#e2b9b962) |`-` |The data of the returned live room. |
|HostInfo |Object of [HostInfo](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/byteplus-livesaas/docs-running-the-demos#fd8b1303) |`-` |The host account information of the returned live room. |


<span id="bb44f8f9"></span>
#### ActivityInfo


|Name |Data Type |Sample Value |Description |
|---|---|---|---|
|ActivityName |String |`Live room A` |The live room name. |
|CoverImageUrl |String |`//example.image` |The URL of the returned live room's cover image in landscape mode.<br><br>If the cover image is set via an API call, the URL includes a protocol header. If set via the console, it does not include a protocol header. |
|VerticalCoverImageUrl |String |`//example.image` |The URL of the returned live room's cover image in portrait mode.<br><br>If the cover image is set via an API call, the URL includes a protocol header. If set via the console, it does not include a protocol header. |
|SdkToken |String |`By****` |The user token in public mode for the Web Viewer SDK.<br><br>When integrating the Web Viewer SDK, set the value of `token` to the current parameter value and the value of `mode` to `1`. |
|Type |Integer |`2` |The status of the returned live room. Valid values:<br><br><br>* `1`: Live. The live video will automatically play.<br><br>* `2`: Preview. If a preview is uploaded, the preview will automatically play. If no preview is uploaded, the cover image will be displayed.<br><br>* `3`: Playback. The playback will automatically play.<br><br>* `4`: Over. The cover image will be displayed. |


<span id="e2b9b962"></span>
#### ActivityData


|Name |Data Type |Sample Value |Description |
|---|---|---|---|
|VirtualPeopleCount |Integer |`100` |The virtual popularity of the returned live room. |


<span id="fd8b1303"></span>
#### HostInfo


|Name |Data Type |Sample Value |Description |
|---|---|---|---|
|HostName |String |`Host A` |The name of the host account. |
|HostAvatarImageUrl |String |`//example.image` |The URL of the host account avatar.<br><br>If the host account avatar is set via an API call, the URL includes a protocol header. If set via the console, it does not include a protocol header. |


<span id="764a79ee"></span>
### Samples

<span id="2469b6d2"></span>
#### Sample request

```JSON
GET /app-server-demo/v2/activity/detail/list?PageNumber=1&PageSize=10&ActivityName=A&ActivityTag=clothes
```


<span id="465196d9"></span>
#### Sample response

```JSON
{
    "PageNumber": 1,
    "PageSize": 10,
    "TotalCount": 1,
    "List": [
        {
            "ActivityId": 17218346****,
            "ActivityInfo": {
                "ActivityName": "Live room A",
                "CoverImageUrl": "//example.image",
                "VerticalCoverImageUrl": "//example.image",
                "SdkToken": "By****",
                "Type": 2
            },
            "ActivityData": {
                "VirtualPeopleCount": 100
            },
            "HostInfo": {
                "HostName": "Host A",
                "HostAvatarImageUrl": "//example.image"
            }
        }
    ]
}
```
